context: The Oct 29 Binance incident spans native XRP, issuer-controlled stablecoins, DeFi collateral and multiple chains. Reported impact, on-chain outflow, issuer freeze, recovered funds and remaining attacker-controlled assets are not interchangeable.
decision: Represent incident data with chain_id, asset_id, token_contract_or_native_asset, source_wallet_entity, destination_entity, amount_native, valuation_timestamp, valuation_usd, evidence_provider, source_cutoff_utc, freeze_state, freeze_authority, recovery_state, exchange_PoR_membership, customer_liability_link, and confidence. Keep native XRP transfers separate from RLUSD/USDC/USDT issuer-freeze events. Keep reported incident impact separate from independently traced outflows and from recovered/restituted amounts.
required_controls: No aggregate USD figure without valuation timestamp and asset/chain breakdown.
Freeze is not recovery; blocked is not returned.
A native XRP transfer is not an XRP sale.
A wallet outflow is not an exchange netflow until wallet/entity mapping is verified.
PoR snapshot membership must be crosswalked by address before computing reserve impact.
Provider attribution is not an official law-enforcement finding.
No event-driven forecast without synchronized market/derivatives/liquidity controls and out-of-sample evaluation.
next_action: Add incident event schema and chain-specific entity/address crosswalk validation to the ingestion and feature-store contracts after the current evidence snapshot is verified.
